newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Crude Outlook - Demand for heavier grades.
newsitem.headline: Asia Crude Outlook - Demand for heavier grades.

text.p: The heavy Asian crude market could see a rise in prices over the next week, as northern Asia moves into the peak demand season.
But ample supplies of light sweet Asian crudes, versus thin buying, were expected to keep Tapis and the Australian crudes under pressure.
June cargoes of light grades such as Kutubu and Thevenard were still on offer.
Traditionally, light Asian crudes start trading a month prior to the loading period, and the market should have already moved into July at this time.
But Australian refiners had been running a heavier crude slate, buying more Minas and Bach Ho, because they are relatively cheaper.
This left the light crude market oversupplied. July demand was expected to offer little respite.

Thailand's 120,000 barrels per day (bpd) Bangchak Petroleum Plc acquired a Murban cargo in its monthly tender last week, rather than a regional light grade. Traditionally, the refiner has bought regioinal light grades in the tender.
Premiums of heavier crudes from Indonesia, China and Vietnam were strengthening because they were more competitive versus grades priced off Dubai, Tapis or Brent, traders said.
Japan and South Korea were offering further support to the heavier market. Refiners and utilities there are gearing up for peak summer demand when air conditioning use rises sharply.
The July market for Middle East crude only started just last week. Trading was expected to pick up through this week as official selling prices are released.
During the weekend, Abu Dhabi released its official retroactive prices for May, raising prices by $1.70/$2.00 per barrel from April.
But the differential between Dubai and ADNOC crudes has narrowed by around 22 cents from the previous month.
Traders said this was a bullish sign and would help counter discounted spot prices of ADNOC crudes.
But the narrower ADNOC-Dubai differential could be offset by reduced buying of ADNOC grades from Japan, where middle distillates stocks are unseasonally high.
Weak margins were also prompting Singapore refiners to consider reducing their refinery runs.
Esso Singapore last week cut crude runs of its 230,000 b/d refinery by 10 percent for an indefinite period.
Most of the Middle East crudes started July trading at low levels.
Murban deals were done at discounts of around 30 cents under the official ADNOC prices, while July Oman was heard sold to China at MPM -15.
